name: Barbell Bench Press
setup: Lie flat on the bench with eyes directly under the bar
Plant feet firmly on the floor
Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and retract shoulder blades
form_cues: Lower bar under control to mid-chest / sternum
Keep wrists stacked over elbows
Drive feet into floor as you press upward
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows out at 90 degrees
Bouncing bar off the sternum
injury_prevention: Tuck elbows to roughly 45-75 degrees to protect the shoulder joint

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
setup: Set bench to 30-45 degree incline
Sit back and kick dumbbells up with knees to shoulders
Retract scapulae and plant feet firmly
form_cues: Press dumbbells up and slightly inward without clanking
Control descent to stretch upper pectorals
Maintain a slight natural arch in the lower back
common_mistakes: Incline set too steep turning into shoulder press
Dropping elbows too low under excessive strain
injury_prevention: Keep dumbbells aligned at 45 degrees rather than straight flared out

name: Cable Chest Fly
setup: Set cable pulleys to chest height or slightly higher
Take one handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance
Maintain a slight bend in both elbows
form_cues: Bring handles together in front of chest in a hugging motion
Squeeze pectorals hard at peak contraction
Control the eccentric stretch slowly
common_mistakes: Bending and extending elbows like a press
Allowing shoulders to roll forward at the stretch
injury_prevention: Do not over-stretch shoulders backward past active chest control

name: Standard Push-Up
setup: Place hands shoulder-width apart on the floor
Extend legs with feet together forming a rigid plank
Engage glutes and core
form_cues: Lower chest until 2-3 inches off the ground
Keep elbows at approximately 45 degrees to the torso
Push the floor away through palms to full lockout
common_mistakes: Sagging lower back or hips
Tucking chin downward to touch chest prematurely
injury_prevention: Maintain full body tension to prevent lumbar hyperextension

name: Chest Dips
setup: Mount parallel dip bars with arms extended
Lean torso forward about 30 degrees
Bend knees and cross ankles
form_cues: Lower down until upper arms are parallel to floor
Maintain forward torso lean throughout
Drive through palms back to top position
common_mistakes: Staying too upright shifting stress entirely to triceps
Dropping too deep causing anterior shoulder impingement
injury_prevention: Stop descent when shoulders reach elbow height to protect AC joints

name: Flat Dumbbell Press
setup: Sit on flat bench with dumbbells resting on thighs
Lie back bringing weights to sides of chest
Set shoulder blades together into the bench
form_cues: Press weights upward converging slightly over mid-chest
Lower with 2-second eccentric phase
Keep forearms perpendicular to the floor
common_mistakes: Letting dumbbells drift toward belly button
Lifting feet off the floor
injury_prevention: Do not let elbows drop significantly below the bench surface

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
setup: Secure shins under decline bench ankle pads
Lie back and grip bar slightly wider than shoulder width
Unrack bar with arms locked
form_cues: Lower bar to lower chest line
Keep elbows at 45 degrees to torso
Press straight up to lockout
common_mistakes: Unracking without a spotter or proper safety catches
Bouncing weight off lower ribs
injury_prevention: Always ensure feet and shins are firmly locked into pads before lifting

name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
setup: Set pulleys to lowest position
Grip D-handles with palms facing up and forward
Step forward with one foot for balance
form_cues: Scoop hands upward and inward toward clavicle height
Squeeze clavicular head of pectorals at top
Lower slowly resisting the cable pull
common_mistakes: Using momentum from lower back extension
Bending elbows into a bicep curl
injury_prevention: Keep core tight and avoid leaning excessively back during upward phase

name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, bar over midfoot
Hinge at hips and grip bar outside legs
Pull chest up, drop hips slightly, and engage lats
form_cues: Push the floor away through midfoot and heels
Keep bar in contact with shins and thighs
Lock out by squeezing glutes at the top
common_mistakes: Rounding the lumbar spine under load
Hyperextending lower back at lockout
injury_prevention: Set back flat before initiating pull; never jerk bar off the floor

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
setup: Stand with barbell over midfoot
Hinge torso forward to roughly 45 degrees with flat back
Grip bar with overhand shoulder-width grip
form_cues: Pull bar toward lower abdomen / navel
Drive elbows back and squeeze scapulae together
Lower under full control without dropping torso
common_mistakes: Using excessive hip drive to heave the weight
Standing too upright turning it into a shrug
injury_prevention: Brace abdominal wall to maintain rigid lumbar spine throughout

name: Pull-Up
setup: Grip pull-up bar with overhand grip wider than shoulders
Hang at full arm extension with engaged shoulders
Cross ankles and tuck pelvis slightly
form_cues: Drive elbows down and back toward your ribs
Pull until chin clears the bar or upper chest touches
Lower under control to full dead hang
common_mistakes: Kipping or swinging legs for momentum
Partial reps failing to achieve full extension
injury_prevention: Control eccentric descent to avoid sudden shoulder jerks at the bottom

name: Cable Lat Pulldown
setup: Adjust thigh pad so legs are locked firmly
Grip wide bar with overhand grip
Sit down, chest lifted with slight backward torso lean
form_cues: Pull bar down smoothly toward upper chest / collarbone
Depress shoulder blades down into back pockets
Slowly extend arms back to starting stretch
common_mistakes: Pulling bar behind the neck
Swinging torso backward to use bodyweight momentum
injury_prevention: Always pull to front of chest to prevent cervical and shoulder strain

name: Seated Cable Row
setup: Sit on cable row bench with feet on footplates and slight knee bend
Grip V-bar handle with both hands
Sit upright with chest tall and spine neutral
form_cues: Pull handle into lower sternum / navel
Retract shoulder blades fully at peak pull
Resist the weight forward without rounding back
common_mistakes: Excessive rocking forward and backward from lower back
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears
injury_prevention: Keep knees slightly bent and spine upright to protect lumbar discs

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
setup: Place knee and same-side hand on flat bench
Opposite foot flat on the floor for sturdy tripod base
Hold dumbbell in free hand hanging directly below shoulder
form_cues: Pull dumbbell toward hip crease driving elbow to ceiling
Keep torso parallel to bench without twisting spine
Lower weight with controlled stretch
common_mistakes: Rotating torso excessively to hoist the weight
Pulling straight up to armpit instead of back toward hip
injury_prevention: Keep supporting arm active and neck neutral with eyes on bench

name: Inverted Bodyweight Row
setup: Set a barbell in a rack at waist height
Lie under bar and grip with overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders
Hang with heels on floor and body in rigid straight plank
form_cues: Pull chest up until it touches or nears the bar
Squeeze shoulder blades hard at top
Lower smoothly to full elbow extension
common_mistakes: Sagging hips during the pull
Reaching neck forward to touch bar
injury_prevention: Keep glutes and abs braced to protect lower back posture

name: Incline Dumbbell Chest-Supported Row
setup: Set bench to 30-45 degree incline
Lie chest-down against pad with feet planted behind
Hold dumbbells hanging naturally below shoulders
form_cues: Pull dumbbells up and back driving elbows past ribs
Pinch shoulder blades together at top contraction
Lower weights slowly to full stretch
common_mistakes: Lifting chest off pad to cheat reps
Jerking neck up during pull
injury_prevention: Keep chest glued to the pad to eliminate lower back spinal load completely

name: Barbell Back Squat
setup: Rest bar on upper traps (high bar) or rear delts (low bar)
Step back, feet shoulder-width apart, toes flared 15-30 degrees
Take deep belly breath and brace core
form_cues: Sit hips down and push knees out tracking toes
Descend until hip crease is at or below knee level
Drive up spreading floor with feet keeping chest proud
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward (valgus collapse)
Heels lifting off the ground during descent
injury_prevention: Maintain neutral lumbar spine throughout; do not let lower back round

name: Barbell Front Squat
setup: Rest bar across front deltoids near throat
Grip with fingertips or cross-arm grip with elbows pointing high
Set stance shoulder-width apart
form_cues: Keep elbows driven up high throughout entire movement
Descend straight down with near-vertical torso
Drive through midfoot to stand up tall
common_mistakes: Letting elbows drop causing bar to slip forward
Collapsing chest forward
injury_prevention: Maintain high elbow drive to keep spine erect and bar secure on shoulders

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
setup: Hold single dumbbell vertically against chest with palms cupping top plate
Set feet shoulder-width apart with slight toe flare
Brace core and keep chest upright
form_cues: Squat down between knees keeping elbows inside thighs at bottom
Hit parallel or deeper with flat feet
Push through heels and midfoot to return to top
common_mistakes: Allowing weight to pull chest forward
Knees tracking inside foot line
injury_prevention: Keep weight firmly pinned against chest to prevent spinal flexion

name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
setup: Stand tall holding dumbbells at sides
Engage core and look forward
Ensure clear straight walking path
form_cues: Take comfortable stride forward landing heel-to-toe
Lower until back knee gently taps or hovers 1 inch above floor
Drive through front heel directly into next stride
common_mistakes: Taking too short a step pushing front knee excessively past toes
Torso leaning forward uncontrollably
injury_prevention: Keep front knee aligned over second toe to protect patellar tendon

name: Bodyweight Air Squat
setup: Stand with feet slightly wider than hips
Extend arms forward for counterbalance
Engage core muscles
form_cues: Hinge hips back and bend knees simultaneously
Descend until thighs break parallel to floor
Drive up evenly through feet to full hip extension
common_mistakes: Initiating movement purely with knees bending forward
Rounding back at bottom
injury_prevention: Keep whole foot rooted to the ground and chest upright

name: Bodyweight Bulgarian Split Squat
setup: Stand 2-3 feet in front of a flat bench
Place top of rear foot laces-down on the bench
Keep hips squared and torso tall
form_cues: Lower hips down and slightly back until front thigh is parallel
Keep front shin relatively vertical
Drive through front foot heel to return to top
common_mistakes: Placing front foot too close to bench jamming knee joint
Tilting hips sideways
injury_prevention: Ensure stable balance before initiating descent to prevent ankle roll

name: Cable Leg Extension
setup: Attach ankle strap to low cable pulley and fasten around right ankle
Sit on bench facing away from cable stack
Grip sides of bench for stability
form_cues: Extend knee until leg is straight out in front
Hold quad contraction at full lockout for 1 second
Lower slowly resisting cable tension back to 90 degrees
common_mistakes: Swinging torso backward to generate momentum
Letting knee hyperextend violently
injury_prevention: Maintain controlled tempo and avoid slamming weights at bottom

name: Cable Squat
setup: Attach straight bar or rope to lowest pulley setting
Grip attachment at chest level and step back 2 feet
Set feet shoulder-width apart
form_cues: Squat down keeping torso upright against the forward cable pull
Descend to parallel thighs
Drive through heels back to standing
common_mistakes: Leaning too far backward relying on cable to hold bodyweight
Letting cable pull shoulders forward
injury_prevention: Keep core tightly braced to counter the horizontal shear force

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
setup: Hold barbell at thighs with overhand grip
Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft (slight bend)
Retract shoulder blades and brace core
form_cues: Hinge hips backward as if touching a wall behind you
Slide bar down thighs keeping it close to shins
Stop when you feel full hamstring stretch and reverse by thrusting hips forward
common_mistakes: Bending knees into a squat
Rounding lower spine as bar travels lower
injury_prevention: Only go as deep as hamstring mobility allows without spinal rounding

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
setup: Hold pair of dumbbells in front of thighs
Stand hip-width with knees slightly unlocked
Engage lats to keep dumbbells close to legs
form_cues: Push hips back smoothly maintaining fixed knee angle
Lower dumbbells down shin level until hamstrings are taut
Squeeze glutes and hamstrings to stand tall
common_mistakes: Letting dumbbells drift away from legs
Rounding shoulders forward
injury_prevention: Keep dumbbells glued to legs to reduce leverage on the lower spine

name: Single-Leg Dumbbell RDL
setup: Stand balancing on right leg with dumbbell in left hand
Keep right knee soft and hips level
Find a focus point on the floor 6 feet ahead
form_cues: Hinge forward sending non-working leg straight back
Lower until torso is nearly parallel to floor
Drive through working foot heel to return upright
common_mistakes: Allowing non-working hip to rotate open toward ceiling
Losing balance by rushing reps
injury_prevention: Keep hips square to floor to avoid torsional stress on sacrum

name: Cable Pull-Through
setup: Attach rope to low pulley
Straddle cable facing away from stack, holding rope between legs
Walk forward a few paces until tension is felt
form_cues: Hinge at hips reaching hands back through legs
Keep back flat and knees soft
Thrust hips forward and squeeze glutes and hamstrings at lockout
common_mistakes: Squatting down instead of hinging back
Pulling with arms instead of driving with hips
injury_prevention: Do not hyperextend spine at top; finish with vertical pelvis

name: Cable Standing Leg Curl
setup: Attach ankle cuff to lowest pulley
Secure cuff to ankle facing the machine
Hold machine frame for steady support
form_cues: Curl heel upward toward glutes
Keep knees aligned with each other
Lower weight with controlled eccentric return
common_mistakes: Swinging knee forward before curling
Arching lower back to hoist the weight
injury_prevention: Keep pelvis neutral and do not jerk weight with hip flexors

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
setup: Kneel on padded surface with ankles secured under sturdy anchor or held by partner
Keep hips fully extended forming straight line from knees to head
Cross arms over chest or keep hands ready to catch floor
form_cues: Lower body forward slowly purely by resisting with hamstrings
Keep hips locked in extension without hinging
Catch yourself with hands on floor when unable to hold
common_mistakes: Breaking at the hips and sticking butt backward
Crashing down onto floor without control
injury_prevention: Use hands to absorb impact at bottom and push back up smoothly

name: Bodyweight Hamstring Bridge
setup: Lie face up on mat with knees bent at roughly 90 degrees
Place heels firmly into floor and toes pointed slightly up
Arms flat at sides for stability
form_cues: Drive heels into floor and bridge hips up toward ceiling
Squeeze hamstrings and glutes hard at the apex
Lower hips down under control to light floor tap
common_mistakes: Over-arching lower back instead of hip extension
Placing feet too close to glutes shifting load to quads
injury_prevention: Brace core to ensure movement comes from hips, not lumbar spine

name: Barbell Good Morning
setup: Rest barbell across upper back / rear delts like a back squat
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees unlocked
Take tight grip and lock lats down
form_cues: Hinge hips backward maintaining flat back
Lower torso toward horizontal until hamstrings stretch
Push hips forward to return to standing position
common_mistakes: Rounding upper or lower spine under load
Bending knees excessively turning it into a squat
injury_prevention: Start with light loading; never allow back to round forward

name: Overhead Barbell Press
setup: Grip bar just outside shoulder width with forearms vertical
Rest bar on front delts / clavicles
Stand with feet hip-width apart and squeeze glutes
form_cues: Press bar straight up moving head slightly back to clear chin
Push head forward through the window once bar clears forehead
Lock out bar directly over midfoot and crown of head
common_mistakes: Excessive backward arching of the lumbar spine
Flaring forearms outward under the bar
injury_prevention: Squeeze glutes and abs hard throughout to prevent lower back hyperextension

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
setup: Sit on upright bench with back firmly supported
Bring dumbbells to shoulder level with palms facing forward or slightly angled
Plant feet flat on the floor
form_cues: Press dumbbells overhead along natural arc until nearly touching
Lower dumbbells under control until elbows reach shoulder height
Keep shoulder blades depressed and stable
common_mistakes: Bouncing weights off shoulders
Arching lower back away from bench pad
injury_prevention: Keep wrists stacked directly over elbows throughout vertical travel

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
setup: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides
Maintain slight bend in elbows and lean forward 5 degrees
Feet hip-width apart with braced core
form_cues: Raise arms out to sides leading with elbows until parallel with floor
Pour pitcher slightly with pinkies slightly higher than thumbs
Lower slowly resisting gravity down to thighs
common_mistakes: Swinging body back and forth for momentum
Shrugging shoulders up using upper traps
injury_prevention: Do not lift above shoulder height in internal rotation to avoid impingement

name: Cable Lateral Raise
setup: Set pulley to lowest level
Stand side-on to pulley and grip handle with far hand behind or in front of body
Maintain slight elbow bend
form_cues: Pull cable diagonally up and out to side until arm is parallel to floor
Focus on medial delt contraction throughout constant tension
Control the descent back to starting point
common_mistakes: Using excessive weight and jerking torso
Bending elbow into a bicep curl
injury_prevention: Keep motion smooth and controlled under continuous cable resistance

name: Cable Face Pull
setup: Attach rope to cable pulley set at eye level
Grip ends of rope with thumbs pointing backward
Step back into staggered stance for solid balance
form_cues: Pull center of rope toward bridge of nose / eyes
Separate rope ends driving thumbs backward into external rotation
Hold peak contraction for 1 second feeling rear delts and rotator cuff
common_mistakes: Pulling down to chest like a row
Leaning torso back and forth
injury_prevention: Emphasize external rotation to promote rotator cuff health and shoulder posture

name: Bodyweight Pike Push-Up
setup: Start in push-up position and walk feet toward hands into inverted V
Hips elevated high toward ceiling with straight legs and arms
Gaze directed back toward feet
form_cues: Lower head forward forming a tripod with hands
Descend until forehead gently touches ground ahead of fingers
Push back and up along diagonal path to full lockout
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring straight sideways
Allowing hips to drop during descent
injury_prevention: Keep elbows angled at 45 degrees relative to shoulders

name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
setup: Hinge forward at hips until torso is nearly parallel to floor
Hold light dumbbells hanging below chest with soft elbows
Neutral spine and flat back
form_cues: Raise arms out to sides pulling with rear deltoids
Lead with elbows and avoid pinching shoulder blades too early
Lower weights smoothly under control
common_mistakes: Using too heavy weights and swinging back
Bending elbows into rows
injury_prevention: Keep lower back flat and supported; use light weights for target activation

name: Wide-Grip Barbell Upright Row
setup: Stand tall holding barbell with wide overhand grip (1.5x shoulder width)
Arms fully extended in front of thighs
Feet shoulder-width apart
form_cues: Pull bar upward along torso leading with elbows
Stop when elbows reach shoulder height
Lower bar under strict control
common_mistakes: Narrow grip that strains wrists and rotator cuff
Pulling bar up to chin causing shoulder impingement
injury_prevention: Always use wide grip and stop at mid-chest height to protect subacromial space

name: Standing Barbell Bicep Curl
setup: Stand upright holding barbell with underhand shoulder-width grip
Pin elbows against your ribcage
Feet hip-width apart with braced core
form_cues: Curl bar upward toward upper chest keeping upper arms stationary
Squeeze biceps firmly at top of rep
Lower bar slowly with 2-3 second eccentric return
common_mistakes: Swinging hips to generate momentum
Letting elbows drift far forward during curl
injury_prevention: Keep torso completely motionless to protect lumbar spine from shear

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
setup: Set incline bench to 45-60 degrees
Sit back with arms hanging straight down holding dumbbells
Keep shoulders pinned back to bench pad
form_cues: Curl dumbbells upward supinating wrists as you lift
Keep elbows pointing at floor to isolate long head stretch
Lower with complete stretch at the bottom
common_mistakes: Lifting shoulders off bench
Swinging elbows forward
injury_prevention: Do not hyperextend elbows under excessive weight at the bottom

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
setup: Stand tall with dumbbells hanging at sides with neutral grip
Keep elbows tucked into sides
Feet planted firmly hip-width apart
form_cues: Curl weights upward keeping palms facing each other
Squeeze brachialis and brachioradialis at top
Lower under strict control to full extension
common_mistakes: Swinging body back and forth
Flaring elbows outward
injury_prevention: Maintain neutral wrist position throughout movement

name: Cable Rope Tricep Pushdown
setup: Attach rope to high pulley
Grip rope with neutral grip and tuck elbows tight to ribs
Lean torso slightly forward 10 degrees
form_cues: Push rope downward extending elbows fully
Spread rope ends apart at bottom for peak triceps contraction
Control return allowing forearms to come back to 90 degrees
common_mistakes: Letting elbows move back and forth with every rep
Using shoulders to push the weight down
injury_prevention: Lock elbow pivot in place to prevent shoulder tendon overload

name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
setup: Set pulley at chest height with rope attachment
Turn away from machine, hold rope behind head, and step into staggered stance
Elevate elbows alongside ears
form_cues: Extend forearms forward and overhead until arms are straight
Keep upper arms fixed in place next to head
Allow deep stretch in triceps long head on eccentric return
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows widely out to the sides
Arching back excessively
injury_prevention: Keep core braced in staggered stance to stabilize lower back

name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
setup: Lie on bench under barbell
Grip bar with shoulder-width grip (hands ~12-14 inches apart)
Set shoulder blades together into bench
form_cues: Lower bar toward lower sternum keeping elbows close to torso
Tuck elbows at 30-45 degrees
Press bar straight up emphasizing triceps lockout
common_mistakes: Grip placed too narrow causing intense wrist strain
Flaring elbows outward
injury_prevention: Keep grip shoulder-width; wrists must stay straight above elbows

name: Bodyweight Bench Dips
setup: Place palms on edge of bench with fingers forward
Extend legs out in front with heels on floor
Keep hips close to the bench edge
form_cues: Lower body by bending elbows back until 90 degree bend
Keep back sliding closely alongside the bench
Press through palms to return to full arm lockout
common_mistakes: Letting hips drift far forward from bench straining anterior shoulders
Dropping below 90 degrees of elbow flexion
injury_prevention: Keep back close to bench to avoid extreme anterior shoulder shear

name: Bodyweight Chin-Up (Underhand)
setup: Grip pull-up bar with underhand (supinated) grip shoulder-width apart
Hang with straight arms and shoulders engaged
Cross ankles and squeeze abs
form_cues: Pull body up driving elbows down and back toward ribs
Bring chin over the bar squeezing biceps at top
Lower under strict control to full dead hang
common_mistakes: Swinging legs or kipping for upward drive
Dropping quickly from top without eccentric resistance
injury_prevention: Control the bottom position to protect the bicep tendon

name: Standard Forearm Plank
setup: Place forearms on floor with elbows directly under shoulders
Extend legs straight back with toes on floor hip-width apart
Neutral head position looking at floor between hands
form_cues: Squeeze glutes, quads, and abdominal wall simultaneously
Maintain rigid straight line from heels to crown of head
Breathe steadily while maintaining intense isometric tension
common_mistakes: Allowing hips to sag toward the floor
Piking hips upward into inverted V
injury_prevention: Actively tuck pelvis (posterior pelvic tilt) to protect lower back

name: Hanging Leg Raise
setup: Hang from pull-up bar with overhand grip and engaged shoulders
Keep legs straight and toes pointed
Engage lats to stabilize body from swinging
form_cues: Roll pelvis up and raise legs toward horizontal or bar level
Focus on abdominal contraction rolling spine up
Lower legs slowly without using swinging momentum
common_mistakes: Using hip flexors only without posterior pelvic tilt
Swinging legs forward and backward for momentum
injury_prevention: Curl pelvis upward to engage rectus abdominis and prevent psoas hyperextension

name: Cable Rotational Woodchopper
setup: Set pulley at shoulder height with single handle
Stand sideways to cable with wide athletic stance holding handle with both hands
Arms extended in front of chest
form_cues: Rotate torso across body driving with hips and core
Pivot on back foot as you rotate through
Return under control resisting the cable stack
common_mistakes: Rotating purely with shoulders and arms instead of torso
Keeping back foot glued flat stressing knee
injury_prevention: Pivot back foot to allow hip rotation and protect knee and lumbar spine

name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
setup: Attach rope to high pulley
Kneel 2 feet in front of stack holding rope ends beside ears
Hips back above heels
form_cues: Crunch downward curling spine bringing elbows toward knees
Keep hips stationary and contract abs hard at bottom
Return slowly allowing abs to stretch under resistance
common_mistakes: Sitting down onto heels turning it into a hip hinge
Pulling with arms instead of flexing spine with abs
injury_prevention: Keep hips locked in space so the movement is pure spinal flexion

name: Barbell Ab Rollout
setup: Kneel on pad with round plates loaded on barbell in front of you
Grip bar with shoulder-width overhand grip
Brace core with slight hollow body posture
form_cues: Roll barbell forward slowly extending hips and arms
Extend out as far as can be controlled without sagging
Pull bar back toward knees using abdominal tension and lats
common_mistakes: Letting lumbar spine sag or hyperextend at the bottom
Leading back with hips first instead of pulling with core
injury_prevention: Stop before lumbar spine extends; maintain posterior pelvic tilt

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
setup: Stand tall holding one dumbbell at side, opposite hand behind ear
Feet hip-width apart and chest tall
Hips squared and stationary
form_cues: Bend torso sideways toward dumbbell side lowering weight to knee level
Engage opposite oblique to pull torso back to upright
Stop when straight; do not over-bend to other side
common_mistakes: Holding dumbbells in both hands creating counterweight
Twisting torso forward or backward during lateral bend
injury_prevention: Only hold a dumbbell in ONE hand to allow true unilateral contraction

name: Dumbbell Russian Twist
setup: Sit on floor with knees bent and feet elevated slightly
Lean torso back 45 degrees holding one dumbbell with both hands
Engage abs to hold V-sit balance
form_cues: Rotate torso smoothly moving dumbbell from hip to hip
Follow dumbbell with eyes and shoulders
Maintain rigid core bracing throughout
common_mistakes: Moving only arms without torso rotation
Slouching lumbar spine into floor
injury_prevention: Keep chest proud and spine neutral to avoid loaded flexion-torsion

name: Bodyweight Dead Bug
setup: Lie on back with arms extended toward ceiling
Raise knees to 90 degrees with shins parallel to floor
Press lower back flat into the ground without gaps
form_cues: Lower opposite arm and opposite leg slowly toward floor
Hover limbs 1 inch off ground while keeping lower back glued to floor
Return to center and switch to other side
common_mistakes: Lower back arching off floor during limb extension
Holding breath during repetition
injury_prevention: If lower back begins to arch, shorten the range of leg extension
